items.title: In-vitro study on the effect of cinnamaldehyde, eugenol and polydatin on the growth of Streptococcus mutans and the formation of dental plaque biofilms.
items.source: PubMed · Pakistan journal of pharmaceutical sciences
items.authors: Zhang T, Tan Y, Shan X, et al.
items.summary: Background: Dental caries are chronic infectious diseases with a high global prevalence. Its pathogenesis is closely related to the adhesion of Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans), formation of dental plaque biofilms and acid production. Currently, only a few types of anticaries drugs are available for clinical use and the long-term use of these drugs can lead to side effects, such as drug resistance and dysbiosis of the oral microbiota. Objectives: Therefore, exploring new, safe and effective anti-caries treatments is an urgent task. Screening antimicrobial drugs from herbal medicines for non-antibiotic treatment of bacteria could provide new solutions to these problems. This study aimed to…

items.title: The impact of periodontitis in cardiac autonomic dysfunction by hrv analysis.
items.authors: Vineetha S, Saravanan A, Jeyabanu M, et al.
items.summary: Introduction: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease damaging the supportive structure of teeth. It has systemic impacts including cardiac autonomic dysfunction. Heart Rate Variability (HRV) measures an objective analysis of the extent of autonomic regulation and where decreased parasympathetic activity coupled with increased sympathetic predominance was determined to correlate well with risk in cardiovascular events. This research ascertains periodontitis and its correlation to autonomic dysfunction by HRV analysis. items.title: Navigating Professional Code of Conduct Among Undergraduate Dental Students in Pakistan: A Qualitative Study.
items.authors: Ali S, Ayub SA, Ahmad S, et al.
items.summary: Background: Professionalism in dentistry extends beyond technical competence to include accountability, respect for patients and colleagues, non-maleficence, informed consent, communication, fairness, and conduct consistent with professional standards. In Pakistan, these expectations are shaped by international bioethical principles, national professional regulation, and local social and religious contexts. Aim: To explore undergraduate dental students' experiences of, or observations of, events they perceived as unethical or inconsistent with professional conduct during clinical/workplace learning, and to understand the forms and meanings of these experiences.
